f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.title: Tron: Ares ? Computer Vision
f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.summary: What does perception look like when it belongs to a machine? That question became the foundation for our work on TRON: Ares, where our team of twenty artists designed and animated more than sixty shots of computer vision and interface systems that visualize the world through the eyes of Ares. Rather than creating traditional HUD graphics, we set out to design machine perception itself. Every frame exists as a living system that continuously scans, tracks, evaluates, and reconstructs reality as streams of computation. Driven by a philosophy of maximum detail, each live action plate was transformed through our custom squarepacking algorithms into a computational lattice capable of analyzing the image at multiple scales simultaneously. Source code, reactive graphics, tracking systems, and layered analysis become different expressions of the same intelligence, revealing a world where every pixel is continuously interpreted and every image is rewritten through the language of the machine.

f4b4bb981e:abb39fac635e1988.title: BLASTEMA
f4b4bb981e:abb39fac635e1988.summary: A blastema is the tissue a body forms to regenerate something it has lost. It is made up of progenitor cells capable, for a time, of changing state and giving rise to something else. They don't have a fixed form yet. They are going to become something different. This project starts there and pushes the idea into a place where biology no longer applies: insects whose tissue, instead of regenerating as insects, begins to behave like plant matter. Lichens, moss, mycelium, fungal fruiting bodies. They are not placed on top. They grow from the same tissue, as if the cell had switched sides. The process: each specimen begins as an image, is reconstructed in 3D, and ultimately becomes a Gaussian Splat rendered in real time through our own GLSL shaders. This is where it truly comes alive. It is no longer a fixed model, but a structure that scatters light and changes according to the viewpoint.

a4977d3fa4:f8ade6ad6434b3e2.title: KwolleM Takes Hypebeast on the Road to Tutto Bene With Porsche
a4977d3fa4:f8ade6ad6434b3e2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f8ade6ad6434b3e2.summary: For a recent installment of DRIVERS, three sportscar owners shared an exclusive look at their love for Porsche, expressing what community and cars mean to them ahead of Sportscar Together Day. Continuing to spotlight the moments that bring fans of the brand together, Hypebeast reunites with KwolleM for Italy’s most picturesque driving event: Tutto Bene. Tucked away in Monte Mottarone in Stresa, Italy, the annual event takes a unique approach to showcasing car culture. Minimizing corporate activations, it allows homegrown communities to experience driving runs and stunts in their truest form. For a new Come with Me feature, the music producer shares a slice of the action at the showcase and all the special Porsche events in between. Setting himself up for the trip, KwolleM picks up Porsche’s 911 GT3 RS with an eye-catching Sportscar Together day livery, a fitting choice for the narrow roads and uphill climbs along the journey. He then heads to a private island in Stresa for a VIP dinner. As well as getting to meet fellow Porsche owners, the dinner brings him into the vast mountainscape that will soon host Tutto Bene. The next day, KwolleM heads to the main event alongside 1,000 other car owners, collectors, and casual enthusiasts. After checking in, he begins by exploring the vehicles on show, ranging from rally cars and hypercars to restomods and custom builds that underscore the breadth of automotive culture.As excitement for the hill climb amps up, KwolleM takes his spot along the 9km stretch that trails from the lake up to the peaks. Here, two-time Le Mans winner Patrick Long gears up in his green-wrapped 911 GT3 Cup, while other drivers take their seats in various Porsche models for the staggering climb.On the final day of the road trip, the producer takes his 911 GT3 RS for one last outing to the Porsche Experience Center in Franciacorta. Coinciding with Sportscar Together Day, KwolleM is one of 14,000 Porsche owners and fans who celebrated the worldwide…

a4977d3fa4:02dd908d30c0a3af.title: G-SHOCK’s 2100 “Luxe Black” Series Delivers Staple Accessories Every Creative Needs
a4977d3fa4:02dd908d30c0a3af.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:02dd908d30c0a3af.summary: Behind every G-SHOCK watch is founder Kikuo Ibe’s ambition to make “a watch that never breaks,” and for its latest release, this approach evolves into the “Luxe Black” series. Maintaining the brand’s signature durability and distinctly structured aesthetic, the series introduces the GM-2100LXB and GA-2100LXB with a refined all-black aesthetic. Taking a closer look, both iterations in the series play with a range of textures. From the matte black dial with a fine-grain surface to the vapor-deposited glass and markers, each component brings a multi-dimensional feel that elevates the foundational design of the boxy 2100 line. As for the “Luxe” element, the brand layers the faces with hints of silver in two iterations and gold in the others. Similar to the dial and bio-based resin band, these metallic tones have a matte finish to round out the refined aesthetic. With the new drop standing out as a modern staple, Hypebeast explores how the 2100 “Luxe Black” series fits into the life of Abu Dhabi-based Osama Mutasem. Captured in a new campaign, the community curator and founder of Hang With Me takes the GA-2100LXB on the go as he visits Al Serkal Avenue and stops off at The Hive.While the watch lends a sleek look that matches Mutasem’s tailored style, its versatility proves to be the highlight of its design. Effortlessly transitioning from meetings with fellow creators to scouting concept stores for fresh inspiration, the model provides the curator with uncompromised reliability and an understated edge of confidence.Discover the campaign in the gallery above and the video below. The G-SHOCK 2100 “Luxe Black” series is now available to buy on the Casio Middle East website and in partner stores across the region. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:5e8174b7a7d1a9bb.title: 424 and DITA Unveil Limited-Edition Artoa.92 Eyewear Collaboration
a4977d3fa4:5e8174b7a7d1a9bb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5e8174b7a7d1a9bb.summary: Summary DITA and 424 have officially released a collaborative edition of the Artoa.92 aviator frameThe release is strictly limited to 100 total pairs split across two exclusive lens colorwaysEach custom-packaged pair comes complete with a piece of sandpaper inviting wearers to distress the titanium frame DITA and 424 have officially launched the 424 x Artoa.92 eyewear collaboration. Designed in Los Angeles and handcrafted in Japan, the limited-edition sunglasses reimagine DITA’s signature titanium aviator silhouette through Guillermo Andrade’s distressed design language.The 424 x Artoa.92 centers on a Japanese-engineered titanium aviator frame, marrying DITA’s precision handwork with 424’s signature Los Angeles attitude. Embodying a design concept titled "Perfection, Disturbed," every pair arrives pristine inside a custom leather case styled after the worn textures found throughout 424’s apparel lines. To personalize each piece over time, the packaging includes an enclosed piece of sandpaper, encouraging the wearer to manually distress and scuff the frame.The release is strictly limited to 100 pairs globally, divided evenly into 50 pairs featuring "Pigeon Blood" lenses and 50 pairs featuring "Smoke" lenses.The 424 x Artoa.92 releases on September 18, 2026, for $595 USD exclusively via DITA, U.S. DITA flagship stores, and the 424 Flagship on Melrose Place in Los Angeles. a4977d3fa4:b341ae475fbae8be.title: Kylian Mbappé Leaves Nike and Joins On to Launch Brand's Football Division
a4977d3fa4:b341ae475fbae8be.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b341ae475fbae8be.summary: Summary Swiss sportswear brand On has officially announced its entry into football alongside star forward Kylian MbappéArsenal legend Thierry Henry has been named Director of Football after working with On on the category launch since 2025On will apply its proprietary LightSpray manufacturing technology to develop elite football footwear and apparel On has officially announced its expansion into football alongside world champion Kylian Mbappé, marking the Swiss sportswear brand's debut in the sport. Under the leadership of Arsenal legend Thierry Henry, who steps in as Director of Football after working behind the scenes since late 2025, the brand aims to combine elite athlete insight with Swiss engineering.The partnership positions Mbappé as he departs Nike, as both a core athlete partner and a global ambassador for movement and performance at On. Working directly with On's product development teams in Zurich, Mbappé will test and refine future football footwear and apparel built around On's proprietary LightSpray™ spray-on textile technology.Reflecting on the partnership, Mbappé stated, “From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game. I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.”Henry will oversee strategic growth, athlete relationships, and product direction for the division. FC Barcelona player Sydney Schertenleib also joins the roster to help shape products designed for the women's game, with the launch campaign captured by photographer Juergen Teller at On Labs in Zurich. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:1a07c4a0f60a331e.title: McDonald’s Puts a Bold Stamp on London Fashion Week With New Accessory
a4977d3fa4:1a07c4a0f60a331e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1a07c4a0f60a331e.summary: McDonald’s has hit the streets of London for Fashion Week with a new must-have accessoryThe McHappy Day® Beanie was first spotted on actor Jenny Walser as she arrived at the Mithridate Show earlier this week. A fully reversible knit hat with McDonald’s signature tones, Walser wore the accessory on the yellow side to bring a touch of color blocking to her fit. Outside 180 The Strand, DJ and model Jordan Mainoo-Hames showcased the hat's versatility by pairing it with his usual sporty stylings on his way to Fashion Week events. From the streets of London to McDonald’s locations across the UK, the wider public can now add the limited-edition accessory to their winter wardrobes by buying it at kiosks in their local McDonald’s restaurant. With every purchase, customers will support the charity’s work helping families with children in hospital by providing free accommodation near their ward.The launch celebrates the restaurant’s new national fundraising day, McHappy Day®, with all proceeds from the beanie going to Ronald McDonald House UK. The 14 Ronald McDonald Houses across the UK support families to alleviate the practical and financial pressures that come with hospital stays. Ahead of the drop, find out how fashion week attendees wore the hat – including presenter Charli Fisher, host Kyle De’Volle and DJ Phoenix Brown – by checking out McDonald’s new paparazzi-style campaign in the gallery above. The McHappy Day® Beanie is available in participating McDonald’s restaurants or via the McDonald’s App while stocks last, for £5 GBP (approx. $7 USD). Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:2ccb63eae9b19454.title: Kith x On Expands the K-Tech Line With the New K-Tech 3
a4977d3fa4:2ccb63eae9b19454.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2ccb63eae9b19454.summary: Name: Kith K-Tech Fall 2026MSRP: $180- 190 USDRelease Date: Available NowWhere to Buy: KithKith and On are expanding their collaborative footwear partnership for Fall 2026 with the introduction of the K-Tech 3, the duo’s first dedicated lifestyle silhouette. Building upon the foundation of their previous releases, the new K-Tech 3 features a highly textured upper crafted from technical woven mesh and layered with premium suede overlays.Two colorways offer markedly different treatments: Ivory/Storm layers creamy mesh and pale suede with yellow-green detailing around the heel and branding, finished by a contrasting teal-toned midsole edge, while Black/Black takes a more understated approach with tonal black mesh, matte suede and matching tooling that lets the differences in texture define the shoe. Co-branding appears across the tongue, footbed and lateral side, with K&K artwork placed medially.The new drop also revisits the earlier K-Tech 1 and K-Tech 2 with new seasonal finishes. a4977d3fa4:7ebcaedd440b52b4.title: Levi’s and sacai Partner for Third Collaborative Denim Collection

a4977d3fa4:ea069eb9248bfe13.title: ROSÉ Debuts “new trick” With an iPhone 18 Pro-Shot Music Video
a4977d3fa4:ea069eb9248bfe13.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ea069eb9248bfe13.summary: Summary ROSÉ returns with “new trick,” a dreamy, guitar-driven alt-pop anthem centered on resilience after heartbreak.Dave Meyers directs its playful, nostalgic music video, filmed entirely on iPhone 18 Pro.The release joins Apple’s ongoing “Shot on iPhone” campaign. ROSÉ returns with “new trick,” an uptempo alt-pop and pop-rock single that trades much of the introspection of her 2024 debut album rosie for something brighter, scrappier and more playful. Co-written with frequent collaborator Amy Allen, the track layers dreamy vocals over distorted electric guitars and a brisk, propulsive rhythm, drawing from the breezy energy of ’90s romantic-comedy soundtracks and the punchier pop-punk of the early 2000s. ROSÉ has described the song as one of the “cutest” things she and Allen have made together, explaining that it emerged at a point when she found herself moving away from the sad songs that had previously defined much of her solo writing. The resulting track embraces that change of perspective, balancing sweetness with a slightly rebellious edge.Lyrically, “new trick” begins from a familiar place of romantic disappointment before quickly reframing heartbreak as something survivable — and even a little absurd. ROSÉ considers the fragility of relationships with the observation that “love is unconditional,” only for that idealism to give way to a more determined outlook as she resolves to “pick my heart off the floor.” Rather than dwelling on loss, the chorus turns recovery into an act of attitude: its titular “new trick” becomes a metaphor for changing the way she reacts to heartache, replacing vulnerability with humor, self-possession and forward momentum. That tonal pivot gives the song much of its charm, presenting resilience not as a heavy emotional breakthrough but as an impulsive, mischievous decision to keep moving.That playful reinvention extends into the accompanying Dave Meyers-directed music video, produced as part of Apple’s latest “Shot on iPhone”…

a4977d3fa4:4205cc7b3a7b1c95.title: Bill Skarsgård Is the Lead Protagonist in Kojima Productions’ ‘PHYSINT'
a4977d3fa4:4205cc7b3a7b1c95.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4205cc7b3a7b1c95.summary: Summary Bill Skarsgård and Charlee Fraser lead Kojima Productions’ PHYSINT .Don Lee and Minami Hamabe join the action-espionage game’s cast.Xbox will publish the project, which remains without a release date. Bill Skarsgård has been confirmed as the lead of PHYSINT, Kojima Productions’ upcoming action-espionage game, with Hideo Kojima revealing the casting during the Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 Broadcast. Best known for his portrayal of Pennywise in the IT films and Welcome to Derry, alongside roles in Nosferatu and John Wick: Chapter 4, the actor will headline an ensemble alongside fellow head Charlee Fraser.Additional cast has also been confirmed, including South Korean action star Don Lee (Ma Dong-seok) and acclaimed Japanese actress Minami Hamabe. Kojima noted that costume fittings, scans and camera tests with the two lead actors had already taken place earlier this year, signaling that performance and likeness capture are underway.First announced in early 2024 as a new action-espionage project, PHYSINT marks Kojima Productions’ third original IP and represents a return to the genre closely associated with Kojima’s earlier work. The creator has characterized the project as the culmination of his four-decade career in games, with the studio aiming to combine cutting-edge technology and a high-profile cast to push the boundaries of action espionage.The project has also undergone a notable shift since its reveal: Xbox was recently confirmed as PHYSINT’s new publishing partner, extending its existing relationship with Kojima Productions on OD – KNOCK. Further casting details are expected as development continues, though neither a release date nor confirmed launch platforms have been announced at this time.📢XBOX Tokyo Game Show 2026 Broadcast UpdateBill Skarsgård is confirmed as the lead role in PHYSINT. a4977d3fa4:d08bf59b2abfa1b1.title: Advisry SS27 'AMERICA, STILL' Is a Three-Act Ode to American Resilience
a4977d3fa4:d08bf59b2abfa1b1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d08bf59b2abfa1b1.summary: Summary Advisry's SS27 collection 'AMERICA, STILL' inspired by James Baldwin, unfolds in three 1970s-inspired acts exploring America's tension between collapse and greatness.The collection moves from distressed denim and trench coats to crocodile capelets and checkerboard suits, ending with sequined and pearl-embellished pieces. Framed through James Baldwin's 1969 voice and told in three acts; reaction, dignity, and transformation, Advisry’s Spring/Summer 2027, ‘AMERICA, STILL’ views today's America through the lens of history.Advisry's creative director and designer, 26-year-old Keith Herron, recognizes that the same pressure that causes collapse has always produced greatness. His latest collection doesn't resolve that tension, it documents it, asking which path we're actually witnessing. The work sits between America's overwhelmingly negative present-day sentiment and the ever-present admiration for its cultural output. Herron’s instinct to defend his country, even amidst the current climate, is what drove ‘AMERICA, STILL’.To unpack that uncertainty, Herron turned to the 1970s — a decade of comparable political and cultural unrest — structuring the show into three acts. The first act drew inspiration from Travis Bickle, the antihero of Taxi Driver, through a distressed denim mini dress, drop-shoulder trench coats, and buckled leather jackets. Act two was based on the era of Muhammad Ali and Malcolm X, with crocodile-leather capelets, boxy tartan vests, and checkerboard suits. The final act turned to optimism, closing with sequined basketball shorts, pearl-embellished jackets, and metallic knit sweaters — suggesting Herron sees a bright future for both his country and for Advisry.The Spring/Summer 2027 show drew a packed house in Manhattan’s Flatiron District, including Public School's Maxwell Osborne and KidSuper's Colm Dillane. On every seat sat a fan printed with a photo of Herron's father as a young boy, fifty years ago — the same retrospective that inspired…

a4977d3fa4:63a7fdbf6f82055b.title: Apple Unveils ‘What Holds Us’ Photography Exhibition, Shot on iPhone 18 Pro
a4977d3fa4:63a7fdbf6f82055b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:63a7fdbf6f82055b.summary: Summary Apple is opening a new art exhibition, titled 'What Holds Us,' in New York CityCurated by Kathy Ryan, the show unveils new work by acclaimed photographers all shot on the new iPhone 8 ProThe exhibition is open from September 18 to 20 in Chelsea, Manhattan, with a live talk from the curator on opening night Apple just keeps upping its photography game. The new iPhone 18 Pro comes equipped with a 48MP Fusion Main camera, dubbed the first of its kind made for photographers, offering users even more creative control with variable aperture. For a better picture of the new device's abilities, Apple has tapped three acclaimed photographers to put those upgrades to the test.Among some of the first to get their hands on the new phone ahead of launch last week, artists Jack Davison, Alex Prager, and Jimmy Chin have created new bodies of work for the exhibition, What Holds Us. “The theme holds a mirror to our increasingly fragmented world,” explains Kathy Ryan, the curator and former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, who worked closely with the artists to realize their unique projects. Open from September 18 through 20 in New York, the showcase spotlights people, ideas, and places that ground humanity and how, per Ryan, "technology rises to the occasion to make it possible."Each vision of connection is just as varied in composition as it is in style. For Chin, an athlete, photographer, and filmmaker, it meant a trip up Canada's Bugaboos with climber Conrad Anker. His photographs move from sweeping composite panoramas to intimate details — Anker’s fingers gripped tight on snowy peaks — and vertiginous views of glacial rivers shot from a helicopter. "In these raw, wild places there is nowhere to hide from yourself."In Davison's work, human connection brought touch and physicality to mind. The photographer, known for dramatic chiaroscuro, turned his lens toward the relationship between clay and people. Visceral and tender, the images on…

a4977d3fa4:66527997ceb08517.title: Kiko Kostadinov and ASICS Close Out Their Tabi Sneaker Series With the LYASA FF II
a4977d3fa4:66527997ceb08517.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:66527997ceb08517.summary: Name: Kiko Kostadinov x ASICS LYASA FF IIColorway: Clay Grey/Jasper Green, Reddish Brown/ASICS BlueSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: September 19Where to Buy: Kiko KostadinovKiko Kostadinov and ASICS are closing out their four-part tabi footwear series with the LYASA FF II Tabi, a hybrid silhouette designed by Laura and Deanna Fanning and first shown during Kiko Kostadinov Womenswear’s Fall/Winter 2026 runway presentation. The sneaker brings two seemingly opposing footwear languages together, combining the refined cues of a traditional brogue at the forefoot with the more technical construction of a trail shoe toward the heel. Its split-toe profile remains the visual anchor, complemented by sculpted paneling, metallic ASICS stripes and a substantial sole unit with a marbled effect.Two colorways are offered: “Clay Grey/Jasper Green” sets a muted grey foundation against flashes of pink and purple mesh and vivid green underfoot, while “Reddish Brown/ASICS Blue” pairs earthy brown leather with contrasting blue mesh accents. Titled Designed to Race: Front Row, the event honed in on the synergy between fashion’s innovative creativity and motorsport’s mechanical ingenuity. With McLaren Mastercard F1 Team Drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, as well as rapper Kojey Radical and celebrity stylist Edie Liberty Rose, stopping by the showcase, the diverse guest list brought tastemakers and prominent figures from the respective industries to celebrate the moment in the futuristic space. a4977d3fa4:367ffb6dd734e76e.title: The S’YTE x MOONSTAR 001 Marks a New Footwear Chapter for Yohji Yamamoto’s Label

a4977d3fa4:367ffb6dd734e76e.summary: Name: S’YTE x MOONSTAR Logo Cotton Canvas Sneakers GC/001Colorway: Black/WhiteSKU: TBCMSRP: ¥29,700 JPY (approx. $191 USD)Release Date: September 19Where to Buy: YOHJI YAMAMOTOS’YTE, the Yohji Yamamoto label built around its “Anti-Mode” philosophy, is entering the footwear realm with the S’YTE x MOONSTAR 001 -- a collaborative sneaker based on MOONSTAR’s heritage GYM CLASSIC.Constructed in Japan from durable cotton canvas, the low-top retains the roomy proportions of the athletic-derived original while introducing S’YTE-specific embroidery at the tongue and branded heel patches. The shoe is produced through MOONSTAR’s FINE VULCANIZED line, using a vulcanization process that bonds the rubber sole to the upper for flexibility and durability, while the upper is shaped and fitted to the insole by hand through the traditional “tsurikomi” process.The Black and White colorways both lean into S’YTE’s characteristically stark palette while reversing their contrasts. The Black edition with a deep black canvas upper, matching black rubber toe cap and sole, offset by crisp white laces and white S’YTE tongue embroidery; its heel carries a tonal black patch finished with contrasting “BLACK IS MODEST” branding.The White version flips the treatment with natural off-white canvas, black laces, black foxing and toe protection, plus a bold vertical black strip running down the heel for a graphic, utilitarian finish. a4977d3fa4:3013c6d7f06f9d54.summary: Name: BROTHER BRIDGE x KAMIYA HENRY BootMSRP: TBCRelease Date: September 19Where to Buy: KAMIYABROTHER BRIDGE and KAMIYA have joined forces on a collaborative boot that reworks the Asakusa-based shoemaker’s signature HENRY through KAMIYA’s vintage-informed design language. a4977d3fa4:fcfa35e674197de8.title: The Realest Auctions Shohei Ohtani's Historic 2025 Tokyo Series Game-Worn Jersey
a4977d3fa4:fcfa35e674197de8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fcfa35e674197de8.summary: Summary The Realest has opened public bidding for Shohei Ohtani's game-worn Los Angeles Dodgers jersey from the 2025 MLB Tokyo Series openerThe collectible features the first Gold MLB Logoman patch ever worn in an official game alongside a rare kanji signature and handwritten inscriptionsBidding for the piece is currently live on TheRealest.com and will officially conclude on October 17, 2026 The Realest has officially launched the auction for the Shohei Ohtani 2025 MLB Tokyo Series Game-Worn Dodgers Jersey. Worn during the March 18, 2025 season opener at the Tokyo Dome, the piece marks the first official Major League Baseball game Ohtani ever played in Japan.The jersey stands out as a historic milestone artifact, carrying the first Gold MLB Logoman patch ever worn in an official game—a designation introduced in 2025 for defending MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year winners. The uniform remains intact with the inaugural gold patch stitched alongside the official 2025 Tokyo Series emblem and the Dodgers' Fernando Valenzuela No. 34 memorial patch.Furthering its individual provenance, Ohtani personally autographed the garment in kanji (大谷翔平) and added handwritten inscriptions reading “Opening Day Tokyo Series,” “GU 3-18-25,” and “NL MVP.” The piece has been verified through MLB's on-field authentication program, photo-matched by SIA Photomatching, and documented via Fanatics Authentic as part of The Realest's Certified evaluation program.Bidding for the Shohei Ohtani 2025 MLB Tokyo Series Game-Worn Jersey is open now at The Realest and will close on Saturday, October 17, 2026. a4977d3fa4:d2d156c3d615c0f0.title: ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Previews Its Gritty Combat and “Showbiz” Gameplay
a4977d3fa4:d2d156c3d615c0f0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d2d156c3d615c0f0.summary: Summary RGG Studio previews Stranger Than Heaven’s opening sequence, historical settings and gritty combat.“Showbiz” adds an entertainment-focused dimension to Makoto Daito’s journey.The multi-era action-adventure launches January 15, 2027. SEGA and Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio have offered an extensive new look at Stranger Than Heaven, unveiling the game’s opening sequence alongside fresh footage during a special Tokyo Game Show 2026 livestream.The opening follows protagonist Makoto Daito as he is accused of murder and pursued by police, with the ensuing confrontation doubling as an introduction to the game’s gritty combat system. The presentation also moves through three of the title’s five historical settings - Kokura, Fukuoka in 1915; Kure, Hiroshima in 1929; and Minami, Osaka in 1943 - while showcasing exploration and period-specific activities.The highlight of the special preview was the first official gameplay look at the core "Showbiz" (Show Business) production system. Operating as a Talent Impresario in 1943 Osaka (Minami), players guide Daito as he gathers musical inspiration across city streets, recruits vocalists and band members, adjusts track arrangements using an in-depth mixing interface, and manages live theatrical stage shows.The studio also detailed its new trigger-based combat system, featuring dual light and heavy attacks alongside a revamped stance-based guard system and showcased beginner-friendly options like the "RGG Special Suit" item. Adding to the fanfare, RGG Studio Executive Director Masayoshi Yokoyama confirmed that a live-action Stranger Than Heaven feature film adaptation is currently in development at Netflix, cementing the project’s multi-platform rollout. a4977d3fa4:dbcf64ba2a1ecde6.title: Samsung Requests Dismissal of Dua Lipa's $15 Million USD Image Lawsuit
a4977d3fa4:dbcf64ba2a1ecde6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:dbcf64ba2a1ecde6.summary: Summary Samsung has asked a California federal judge to dismiss Dua Lipa's $15 million USD lawsuit over her photo appearing on TV packagingLegal counsel for the company contends that a celebrity's face does not serve as a trademark or brand endorsement indicatorJudge Christina A. Snyder is scheduled to hear Samsung's motion to dismiss the lawsuit on December 14, 2026 Samsung Electronics has officially filed a motion to dismiss Dua Lipa's $15 million USD lawsuit regarding the unauthorized use of her photograph on television packaging. The filing submitted to the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California argues that the pop star cannot assert trademark rights over her own face.The legal dispute stems from a registered 2024 Austin City Limits backstage photograph displaying Lipa within a mock-up screen interface on Samsung retail boxes. Lipa claims the packaging falsely implies a commercial partnership and product endorsement. In response, Samsung argues that the image serves merely as a background graphic for a music video channel interface rather than a source-identifying trademark, referencing legal precedent involving Tiger Woods and Bob Marley.Samsung further challenges the lawsuit's right-of-publicity claims, arguing that Lipa's United Kingdom domicile renders California publicity laws inapplicable. Additionally, defense lawyers contend the complaint improperly conflates South Korean parent company Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. with its American subsidiary without identifying specific corporate liability. Judge Christina A. Snyder will hear the motion to dismiss on December 14, 2026. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:18f5a16821acf7b2.title: Apple TV Debuts Official Trailer for Mount Everest Drama 'Tenzing' Starring Tom Hiddleston
a4977d3fa4:18f5a16821acf7b2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:18f5a16821acf7b2.summary: Summary Apple Original Films has released the first trailer for Tenzing an adventure drama directed by Jennifer Peedom The narrative centers on Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary during their historic 1953 Mount Everest expedition The film opens in select theaters on October 9 2026 before streaming globally on Apple TV on October 16, 2026 Apple has officially unveiled the official trailer for Tenzing, an upcoming adventure drama directed by Jennifer Peedom. The feature focuses on Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok) and Sir Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) as they attempt the historic first summit of Mount Everest.The narrative emphasizes the cultural and spiritual dimensions of the 1953 expedition, framing Norgay's deep personal connection to the mountain, known in Tibetan culture as Chomolungma. Co-starring Willem Dafoe as expedition leader John Hunt alongside Tenzin Jigmey, Harry Greenwood, and Pasang Arya Sherpa, the film examines Norgay's journey as an outsider establishing his place within the British climbing team.Building on themes from her 2015 documentary Sherpa, Peedom structured the story around faith, belonging, and partnership rather than pure physical conquest. The production incorporated consultations with the late Kanchha Sherpa—the last surviving member of the original 1953 climb—while highlighting Hillary's lifelong commitment to building infrastructure and schools across the Khumbu region alongside Norgay.Tenzing will open in select theaters on October 9, 2026, before debuting globally on Apple TV on October 16, 2026. a4977d3fa4:9598df9750f7f5ec.title: Alexandre Arnault Joins Nike Board of Directors Amid Corporate Restructuring
a4977d3fa4:9598df9750f7f5ec.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9598df9750f7f5ec.summary: Summary Alexandre Arnault has been officially appointed to Nike's board of directorsThe LVMH executive previously held leadership roles at Moët Hennessy Tiffany & Co and RimowaThe move comes as Nike faces financial headwinds and prepares to leave the S&P 100 index on September 21, 2026 Nike has officially appointed LVMH executive Alexandre Arnault to its board of directors. The strategic appointment comes as the sportswear giant navigates a challenging financial period, with company shares falling more than 40% in 2026.Nike President and Chief Executive Elliott Hill highlighted Arnault’s extensive background across brand building, digital transformation, and product innovation as key assets for the company's next phase of growth. Arnault, who has served as deputy chief executive of Moët Hennessy since February 2025 and previously led Rimowa and Tiffany & Co., joins a board that also includes former Apple CEO Tim Cook.The executive addition coincides with major index changes for the sportswear manufacturer. Nike is set to be removed from the S&P 100 index next week, concluding an 18-year run on the blue-chip index that began in December 2008. fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.title: Diffusion of tacit knowledge in a company: a mathematical model based on diffusion on graphs
fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.author: Andrzej Buszko
fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.summary: This article is devoted to the process of diffusing tacit knowledge. This intangible asset has proven crucial for achieving a competitive advantage among market-oriented companies. A novel model of tacit knowledge diffusion is presented, employing the concept of heat diffusion from physics. Furthermore, graph theory and the dynamics it defines are utilized. We defined a Tacit Knowledge Transfer Graph that encodes data from questionnaires. It enables us to identify employees' learning needs, allowing for the planning of classes within the same period, such as a day, to schedule them optimally. Moreover, the model can be used to identify employees with high knowledge demands. The application is not limited to companies; a simple example of planning classes in a school/university is provided. The presented model can help with optimal scheduling, enhance operational efficiency, and improve talent management within the company. It can also identify risks associated with critical sources of knowledge and help improve organizational culture and knowledge management policy.

fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.title: Corporate research and value creation in Peru
fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.author: Iglesias-Osores, Sebastian
fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.summary: This working paper develops a conceptual and contextual framework for understanding corporate research in Peru as a value-creation capability rather than as an activity mainly induced by public grants or tax incentives. The central argument is that public innovation funds and tax benefits can accelerate business innovation, but they cannot substitute for the internal routines through which firms learn, document, protect, and capture value from knowledge. Drawing on the resource-based view, the knowledge-based theory of the firm, absorptive capacity, dynamic capabilities, open innovation, technological capability accumulation in emerging economies, and the appropriability literature, the paper proposes an integrated pathway linking corporate research, structured learning, firm-specific know-how, appropriability decisions, innovation capability, and economic value capture. The argument is situated in the Peruvian context through indicators of low R&D intensity, public information on Law No. 30309, patenting evidence, and sectoral illustrative cases. The paper contributes by reframing public innovation instruments as levers of pre-existing capabilities rather than substitutes for strategy, and by offering a practical maturity framework for managers seeking to transform research activities into intangible assets, technical reputation, and new sources of income.

fc066e842d:f44911270f6ef31a.title: Smarter Bridges: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Reshape University-Industry Technology Transfer
fc066e842d:f44911270f6ef31a.author: Fekkak Hamdi
fc066e842d:f44911270f6ef31a.summary: University-industry technology transfer (UITT) is essential for converting academic research into commercial use, yet traditional strategies often fail to address the knowledge gap. Literature suggests that institutional inertia, communication barriers, and ineffective marketing strategies hinder the commercialization of technology. This study proposes a conceptual framework that incorporates AI-driven marketing to enhance knowledge dissemination, market identification, and stakeholder engagement within the technology transfer process. This systematic literature review amalgamates insights from UITT, AI marketing applications, and knowledge management systems. A qualitative analysis of peer-reviewed literature from 2017 to 2025 identifies trends, deficiencies, and emerging patterns, leading to an integrated framework that assesses technology transfer strategies and the implementation of AI marketing across diverse sectors, leveraging the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). The investigation demonstrates that AI-enhanced marketing can significantly bolster UITT through five AI-enhanced marketing capabilities: precise client segmentation, predictive analytics of market trends, tailored communication, improved knowledge management, and streamlined digital outreach. This methodology fosters reciprocal knowledge exchanges, positioning AI as a facilitator between market insights and university research aims while refining technology presentations for industry stakeholders. Moreover, the study highlights critical concerns regarding data privacy, implementation expenses, technical complexities, and the necessary proficiency in AI and technology transfer.

fc066e842d:a13066ab221da6ad.title: Facets of Human–AI Collaboration: The Importance of Collaboration Type, Invocation Type, and AI Output Quality
fc066e842d:a13066ab221da6ad.author: Diebel, Christopher
fc066e842d:a13066ab221da6ad.summary: Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have made human–AI collaboration increasingly relevant in organizations across various industries. AI-based agents are able to act autonomously, learn from experience, and often outperform humans when solving problems. Moreover, they can generate content indistinguishable from that of human experts and interact in a conversational manner. The advanced capabilities of AI-based agents make human–AI collaboration a promising way for organizations to increase their productivity and performance. Due to this potential, human–AI collaboration has already established itself in several industries and proven to be effective. In software development, AI-based agents can support developers in writing computer code. In financial services, AI-based agents are utilized to make market predictions, and in healthcare, AI-based agents can enhance diagnosis by analyzing patient data. Notably, human–AI collaborations can take multiple forms that differ across several facets, including how responsibilities are distributed between humans and AI-based agents, how the collaboration is invoked, or the quality of the AI-generated output. However, while human–AI collaboration can increase productivity, improve decision-making, or enhance overall performance, previous research has demonstrated that collaborating with AI-based agents can have significant effects on humans in various forms. It is therefore important to understand how the different facets of human–AI collaborations influence the humans involved, to fully realize the potential of such collaboration. Consequently, this thesis aims to investigate how various facets of human–AI collaboration, specifically the type of collaboration, the type of invocation to collaborate, and the quality of output of the AI-based agent within the collaboration (i.e., quality of AI output), can affect humans involved in or affected by the outcomes of such collaborations. fc066e842d:255faef4b8bca7aa.title: Le rôle de la communauté de pratiques dans la création des connaissances : enseignements d'une étude de cas multiple dans le secteur automobile
fc066e842d:255faef4b8bca7aa.author: Mohamed-Larbi Aribou
fc066e842d:255faef4b8bca7aa.summary: In many contexts, organizational knowledge creation emerges as a major strategic lever for sustaining firms' competitive advantage. However, its effectiveness remains strongly conditioned by the organizational context, and more specifically by communities of practice, which influence the processes of knowledge creation, sharing, and integration. This research adopts a qualitative methodology conducted across three companies in the automotive sector, based on 42 interviews, in order to highlight the key role of communities of practice in the creation of new knowledge. The findings show that community dynamics grounded in the mobilization of "soft" factors foster the emergence of new knowledge, whereas those primarily based on technical factors tend to focus on compliance with existing standards, thereby limiting knowledge creation processes.

5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lawrence F. Katz1 1 Harvard University (email: lkatz@harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. Customized housing mobility services combined with subsidized housing vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas. Place-based policies that create mixed-income neighborhoods appear to increase long-term outcomes for less-advantaged children. (JEL I12, I32, I38, J13, J15, R23, R38)

5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andreas Haupt1 and Zoë Hitzig2 1 Stanford Digital Economy Lab (email: h4upt@stanford.edu) 2 Harvard Society of Fellows (email: zhitzig@g.harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. Contextual privacy violations arise when a choice rule makes some agents collectively, but not individually, pivotal. In auctions, designing for contextual privacy requires choosing an initial question posed to each agent and the order for querying agents. Ascending-join protocols are maximally contextually private for k-item Vickrey auctions. (JEL D44, D82)

5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Björkegren1, Joshua E. Blumenstock2 and Samsun Knight3 1 Columbia University (email: dan@bjorkegren.com) 2 UC Berkeley (email: jblumenstock@berkeley.edu) 3 University of…
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment in Kenya. When implemented, linear strategy-robust decision rules outperform standard linear models such as LASSO. (JEL C45, C93, D12, D91, G51, O12, O16)

5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Ethan Ligon1 1 University of California, Berkeley (email: ligon@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. Risk-sharing tests using total expenditures work for idiosyncratic shocks (budgets change, but not prices), but not “covariate” shocks (prices change). I describe all preferences that permit one to infer MUEs from expenditures and estimate nonhomothetic MUEs to test whether covariate shocks are shared efficiently in Uganda. This delivers sensible results; the standard approach suggests that droughts, floods, and pests are beneficial. (JEL D12, D81, O12, O13, Q12)

5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Gabriel Kreindler1, Arya Gaduh2, Tilman Graff3, Rema Hanna4 and Benjamin A. Olken5 1 Harvard University (email: gkreindler@g.harvard.edu) 2 University of Arkansas (email:…
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. Commuters in Jakarta are 2–3 times more sensitive to wait time than bus time and inattentive to long routes. We develop a flexible framework to characterize optimal networks. A less concentrated network would increase ridership and commuter welfare. (JEL L92, L98, O18, R41, R42, R48)

5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.author: info@aeaweb.org (Patrick J. Kennedy1, Christine L. Dobridge2, Paul Landefeld3 and Jacob Mortenson4 1 UCLA, NBER, and JCT (email: pkennedy@econ.ucla.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Board (email:…
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. In the short run, 87 percent of private income gains flow to the top 10 percent of the income distribution. (JEL D22, D31, G31, H25, H32, J23, L25)

5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.author: info@aeaweb.org (Alberto Bisin1 and Giulia Tura2 1 New York University (email: alberto.bisin@nyu.edu) 2 LUISS University (email: gtura@luiss.it))
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. Structural estimates reveal a strong demand to preserve cultural identity on the part of immigrants and limited acceptance of the immigrants' cultural diversity on the part of natives. Furthermore, these estimates reveal a substantial heterogeneity of the parental value of children's education across cultures. Nonetheless, our estimates simulate substantial—though heterogeneous—cultural integration rates across immigrant groups. (JEL D13, J12, J13, J15, Z13)

5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.author: info@aeaweb.org (Amanda Dahlstrand1 1 University of Zurich (email: amanda.dahlstrand@econ.uzh.ch))
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). I find limited trade-offs in matching; horizontal differentiation among doctors and varied patient needs allow improvement in multiple outcomes simultaneously. Efficiency-enhancing reallocations also affect equity. The findings highlight the potential for care reorganization aligning provider heterogeneity with patient needs when geographic constraints are lifted. (JEL C78, H51, I11, I13, I14, I18)

5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.author: info@aeaweb.org (Luigi Iovino1, Thorsten Martin2 and Julien Sauvagnat3 1 Bocconi University (email: luigi.iovino@unibocconi.it) 2 Frankfurt School of Finance and Management (email: t.martin@fs.de) 3…
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. We develop a multisector general equilibrium model that accounts for our evidence and quantify the impact of corporate tax reforms on aggregate emissions. A policy that eliminates the tax advantage of debt could reduce aggregate emissions without affecting GDP. (JEL D22, G32, H25, H32, Q52, Q54, Q58)

5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.title: Rationing by Race
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.author: info@aeaweb.org (Manasvini Singh1 and Atheendar Venkataramani2 1 Carnegie Mellon University and NBER (email: msingh01@cmu.edu) 2 University of Pennsylvania and NBER (email:…
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. These findings are not explained by differential patient selection. We identify rationing by wait times as a mechanism, documenting that sicker Black patients wait longer for care than healthier White patients at almost all capacity levels. Text analysis of unstructured clinical notes reveals rationing of provider effort as another mechanism. (JEL I11, I12, I14, J15)

5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.title: Intergenerational Impacts of Secondary Education: Experimental Evidence from Ghana
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Esther Duflo1, Pascaline Dupas2, Elizabeth Spelke3 and Mark Walsh4 1 MIT and Collège de France (email: eduflo@mit.edu) 2 Princeton University (email: pdupas@princeton.edu) 3 Harvard…
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. We also document cognitive development gains of 0.24 standard deviations of test scores by age five among children of female scholarship recipients. Means-tested secondary school scholarships are a high-return investment, with a conservatively estimated US$4.1 in benefits for each US$1 the policy would cost the government in the long run. (JEL H52, I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, O15)

21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.title: Experimenting on the psychology of LLMs
21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.summary: As LLMs become increasingly important, we're starting to see experiments that explore their psychology. (I expect that Susan Calvin, who was Isaac Asimov's fictional robopsychologist from the1950 short story collection I Robot , will soon have scientists following in her footsteps.) Note that experiments intended to explore A.I. psychology need not necessarily resemble those intended to explore human psychology. Here's an example, from the journal Artificial Intelligence and the Law: Human realignment: An empirical study of LLMs as legal decision-aids in moral dilemmas by Christoph Engel · Yoan Hermstrüwer · Alison Kim Abstract: Recent advances in AI make it conceivable to delegate legal decision-making to machines, or to enhance human adjudication through AI assistance. Using classic normative conflicts — the trolley problem and comparable moral dilemmas — as a proof of concept, we examine the alignment between AI legal reasoning and human judgment. In our baseline experiment, we find a pronounced mismatch between decisions made by GPT and those of human subjects. This misalignment raises substantive concerns for AI-powered legal decision-aids. We investigate whether explicit normative guidance can address this misalignment, with mixed results. GPT-3.5 is susceptible to such intervention, but frequently refuses to decide when faced with a moral dilemma. GPT-4 is outright utilitarian, and essentially ignores the instruction to decide on deontological grounds. GPT-o3-mini faithfully implements this instruction, but is unwilling to balance deontological and utilitarian concerns if instructed to do so. We replicate the experiment with four LLMs from different providers. Claude-sonnet-4.6 comes closest to human respondents. Gemini-2.5-flash-lite is most sensitive to normative instructions. Llama-4-scout and Mistral-nemo have a strong utilitarian bias, and do not strongly respond to normative interventions. At least for the time being, explicit normative instructions…

21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.title: Xenotransplants will substitute for dialysis before they replace human kidney transplants
21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.summary: Transplants of organs from genetically modified pigs to humans is making progress, but pig organs haven't yet survived long enough to be a viable substitute for human organs. Kidneys are a good experimental organ to work with, because when the pig organ fails, the patient can go back on dialysis (and continue to wait for a deceased-donor organ transplant). But if pig organs can last long enough, they might replace dialysis. The first pig-organ recipient to go straight to a human organ transplant has now been reported, in a press release accompanying the case report. Below are both the press release and the case report. Patient Who Received Pig Kidney Becomes First To Progress to Human Kidney Transplant Study shows xenotransplantation can serve as a bridge for patients with end-stage kidney disease By MASS GENERAL BRIGHAM COMMUNICATIONS September 3, 2026 Riella L, Borges T, Rosales I et al. Porcine kidney xenotransplantation as a bridge to allotransplantation: a first-in-human study The Lancet, 2026; "This case shows that porcine kidney xenotransplantation can provide prolonged renal support and be discontinued without clinically significant allosensitisation or zoonotic infection. Early cellular rejection resolved with treatment, whereas later graft failure was associated with microvascular injury progressing to thrombotic microangiopathy despite a negative donor-specific crossmatch, supporting the possibility that mechanisms beyond conventional antibody-mediated rejection contributed to late graft injury. Kidney xenotransplantation has the potential to provide prolonged dialysis-free support while also serving as a bridge to subsequent human allotransplantation ."

21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.title: How to Get Away with Merger in a Dialysis Duopoly by T.G. Wollman
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.summary: Here's a paper featured by Microeconomic Insights, which shows that in the highly concentrated dialysis market, in which prices are mostly federally regulated, mergers reduce competition on quality. Thomas G. Wollmann: How to Get Away with Merger: Stealth Consolidation and Its Effects on US Dialysis "This paper studies premerger notification of US dialysis acquisitions from 1996 to 2017. Like many industries, dialysis has consolidated rapidly. During this period, thousands of facilities changed ownership, yet only half were reported to federal antitrust authorities. Unlike most industries, dialysis prices are mostly set by the government, so acquisitions of rival facilities reduce the incentive to compete on quality. Since patients are often already in poor health, preventing stealth consolidation could save lives. The study combines data on market structure, antitrust enforcement, and patient health. I begin by describing patterns in the data. Next, I estimate a structural model of dialysis competition, enforcement, and agency costs. Finally, I use the estimates to predict what would have happened had all dialysis mergers proposed during the study period been reportable. Three main findings emerge. Premerger notification is critical to effective antitrust enforcement. All else equal, exemption reduces the likelihood of enforcement by about 90%. Exempt acquisitions that concentrate ownership degrade quality, as evidenced by higher postmerger hospitalization and mortality rates. The benefits of expanding premerger notification exceed the costs by orders of magnitude. This reflects the deterrence effect of antitrust enforcement (i.e., rivals won’t try to merge if they know their deal will be blocked) as well as the efficiency of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), which polices billions of dollars of dialysis transactions with very few resources."

21113a7a19:b905bc58f996e177.summary: Privacy while driving seems to be more important than privacy while surfing the internet, to judge from recent reactions to automated license-plate readers produced by the company Flock Safety. Here's the story from the Atlantic: Why the Flock Backlash Has Gotten So Intense The sudden anger about these cameras seems to reflect more than just wariness about the surveillance system. By David A. Graham "As corporate names go, Flock is cleverly flexible. It evokes the many cameras that compose the company’s surveillance system and also a group of sheep, protected by a watchful shepherd. The recent backlash against the company, however, more closely resembles a flight of starlings, seeming to erupt out of nowhere and move as one unified body. ... "Flock is useful because it is ubiquitous. Reforms such as strict data-retention limits would only marginally answer privacy concerns, and anything more drastic would undermine the system’s efficacy. As National Review’s Charles C. W. Cooke noted, no one doubts that Flock works. “ Lots of things would reduce crime if implemented ,” he wrote. “That doesn’t mean that those things are necessarily a good idea in a free republic.” Impositions on privacy to reduce crime are a particularly tough sell when crime is dropping sharply: Recently released FBI statistics show that violent crime dropped nearly 10 percent last year, part of a consistent trend since it spiked in 2020 and 2021. Preliminary statistics suggest that 2026 might be even safer. When safety is a less urgent concern, people are less willing to sacrifice privacy for security. View Paper Presented by: Charles D. Sprenger (California Institute of Technology) Camila Farres (California Institute of Technology), Ted O’Donoghue (Cornell University) We conduct a comprehensive experiment on decision-making for binary lotteries—specifically, lotteries that yield a positive amount or zero. Such lotteries form the basis of many empirical results revealing violations of expected utility (EU) and motivating behavioral alternatives. However, the space of binary lotteries has not been comprehensively explored, and thus the predictions of various behavioral alternatives to EU have not been fully assessed even within this limited domain. We provide this exploration, and discover empirical patterns that stand in stark contrast to the predictions of existing behavioral models. In particular, the data indicate that risk attitudes are driven largely by relative probability comparisons between two options, with absolute magnitudes of probabilities playing a minor role. 21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.title: Three takeaways on Moral Economics, with Lynn Thoman
21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.summary: Lynn Thoman and I discuss three takeaways from Moral Economics (and hers are different than mine): You can listen here: Why Doing the “Right Thing” Can Make Everything Worse and you can watch as well as listen here: "What can we do when doing the morally “right” thing produces worse outcomes? And what if some of society’s strongest moral instincts are preventing us from solving problems we all agree are terrible? Alvin Roth is a Stanford professor and Nobel Prize-winning economist whose work has helped redesign real-world systems, including kidney exchanges and the way doctors are matched with hospitals. His new book, Moral Economics, tackles a harder category of problems: markets and behaviors we find morally objectionable, even when banning them may create consequences we don’t want. He discusses: Why nearly 100,000 Americans can be waiting for a kidney What prohibitions of alcohol and heroin can teach us What happened when Rhode Island accidentally legalized indoor prostitution Whether paying kidney donors could save lives without creating an ethically unacceptable market Why evidence becomes especially important when reasonable people disagree about morality Whether performance-enhancing drugs could eventually become as ordinary as coffee Some policies sound obviously right when judged by their intentions. But what happens when you judge them by their actual consequences? Roth pushes into the uncomfortable territory between those two questions: when banning something creates a black market, when changing a rule may save more lives than inventing a new technology, and what we should do when the outcome we believe is morally necessary turns out to be something we cannot actually achieve."

21113a7a19:5eca3d944980dd90.title: Market design from the Perspective of Theological Anthropology, by Christina McRorie (in the January 2027 ASSA program)
21113a7a19:5eca3d944980dd90.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:5eca3d944980dd90.summary: I'm always on the lookout for different perspectives on market design, and here's a paper that caught my eye in the ASSA Preliminary Program for the January 2027 meetings in Washington DC. It's in a session called What Economic Models Can and Cannot See: Human Flourishing, Freedom, and the Common Good (B4 ) Hosted by the Association of Christian Economists Can Market Design Make Us More Free? Some Notes on the Use of Experimental Economics from the Perspective of Theological Anthropology by Christina McRorie , Boston College Abstract Although modern thought tends to construe freedom as freedom from constraint or freedom of choice, Catholic theological anthropology has long defined true freedom as the state of being agentially oriented toward the good. As Servais Pinckaers puts it, it is “freedom for,” rather than “freedom from”—specifically, freedom for living in a Christ-like way, which becomes possible as we come to participate in Christ’s character. This perspective suggests that social influences which encourage our growth in character are not only helping us become more good, but also more free. Moreover, because this conception of freedom is not based in autonomy, this remains true even if these formative influences are not chosen by us, and work on us without our awareness. Using this concept of freedom, this paper considers the theological implications of experimental research on prosocial behavior in markets. It appears that certain conditions encourage subjects to act with more fairness, trustworthiness, and even generosity than they might under other conditions. (E.g., when market participants can observe each other’s behavior and communicate, and when the social framing of various options emphasizes values, or at least does not emphasize competition or the threat of loss, among other factors.) Insofar as laboratory studies replicate conditions present in actual markets, this indicates that some real markets elicit more moral behaviors than others.…

21113a7a19:c3993e442ea33cf6.title: Axel Ockenfels, interviewed about market design
21113a7a19:c3993e442ea33cf6.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:c3993e442ea33cf6.summary: Here's a recent interview of Axel Ockenfels, about market design. Interview Marc Kley 1. Professor Ockenfels, your work focuses on the design of markets and incentives. How can founders leverage your scientific insights when developing their business models? Every business model is, to some extent, an exercise in incentive and market design, whether founders are aware of it or not. Whoever builds a platform, a pricing scheme or an app decides who can trade with whom, what information they see, and what incentives they face. Market design research offers three lessons for founders. First, details matter: seemingly minor rules can make or break a market. I have seen many systems fail because of seemingly innocuous design mistakes. Second, behavior matters: people reciprocate, care about fairness, are loss averse, and are quickly overwhelmed by complexity. Third, testing matters: experiments are the wind tunnel of market design and the gold standard for finding out what works and what does not. ... 4. In your opinion, which major societal challenge could be solved more effectively if we designed markets, platforms, and incentives more intelligently? Almost any. Take climate change. It is often framed as a moral problem, but at its core it is a cooperation problem: everyone benefits if emissions fall, yet each country, company and individual prefers others to bear the cost. A uniform carbon price would steer billions of everyday decisions toward climate protection without micromanaging any of them. Not less importantly, our research shows that carbon pricing facilitates international negotiations built on reciprocity, which can stabilize cooperation where unilateral pledges fail. A similar logic creates value elsewhere: kidney exchange programs save lives, well-designed electricity markets keep the energy transition affordable, and clever matching systems allocate school places more fairly. Wherever incentives are misaligned, better economic design can unlock large…

2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.title: Debt and Taxes: The Role of Tax Avoidance
2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.author: Brok, Peter
2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.summary: Empirically, the effect of corporate tax rates on leverage has been smaller than expected based on trade-off theory. In this article, I show that tax avoidance functions as a non-debt tax shield, reducing the benefits of the debt tax shield. I find that higher tax rates cause higher non-debt tax avoidance, which crowds out the debt tax shield. Moreover, I show that the strength of the relationship between debt and tax rates depends on the level of tax avoidance. A 1-standard-deviation higher tax rate implies 2.8% higher leverage for low tax avoidance firms, but has a negative effect for high tax avoidance firms.

2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.title: Women in Politics: The Effect on Board Diversity
2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.author: Pareek, Ankur
2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.summary: We use a sharp regression discontinuity design (RDD) to show that victories by women candidates in close House, Senate, and gubernatorial elections lead to an increase in female directors in firms located in the candidates’ districts. The causal effect is higher when the media coverage of the woman candidate is higher, when voter turnout is high, and when firms have more local directors and local institutional investors. The heterogeneous regression discontinuity (RD) effects suggest that electoral wins may influence local gender norms and firms’ board diversity through multiple channels, including conveying majority views on gender-related social norms, increasing exposure to exemplar women, and facilitating learning about women’s different but effective leadership styles. The evidence suggests a potential spillover effect from women’s political leadership to the corporate world.

2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.title: Climate-Triggered Institutional Price Pressure: Does It Affect Firms’ Cost of Equity?
2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.author: Xue, Cheng
2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.summary: We document that climate-triggered institutional portfolio rebalancing affects S&P 500 firms’ cost of equity through climate change price pressure (CCPP). Using a demand-based asset pricing framework, we estimate firm-level CCPP from physical and transition exposures over 2005–2021. A one-standard-deviation intensification of CCPP raises the cost of equity by up to 6% of its average, with banks and insurers as the main drivers. Yet firms do not subsequently improve environmental performance, indicating that the statistically significant effect of CCPP on cost of equity is ineffective to alter corporate behavior. Our CCPP metrics can help policymakers and investors design targeted environmental strategies.

2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.title: Do Shareholder Leverage Constraints Affect Debtholders?
2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.author: Zhang, Lei
2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.summary: We examine the relationship between shareholder leverage constraints and corporate risk-taking, focusing on its impact on debtholders. Our findings show that mutual fund leverage constraints are related to more risk-taking activities of portfolio companies, inducing higher credit risk and greater risk-shifting concerns for the firms’ debtholders. In response, the debtholders raise borrowing costs and tighten lending conditions. These effects intensify for firms facing higher levels of conflict between debtholders and shareholders and when mutual funds exert greater influence over firms.
